compartida: Buying board games and having time to play them are two completely different hobbies. Don't break my heart.
My head says: 'Not one more box fits on that shelf'. My heart says: 'If you stack the boxes vertically, we can squeeze in the Kickstarter that ships next month'.
Growing up is going from 'Which club is open tonight?' to 'Who's reading the 40-page rulebook and explaining it to us in five minutes?'.
My living room isn't a mess, I'm setting up a Big Box game. It's art, you wouldn't get it.
Friends come and go, but victory points stay in your soul for the rest of your life.
You don't know betrayal until your best friend steals the last resource on the final round. That's where diplomacy ends.
A co-op game is that beautiful place where we can all lose together and blame the same spaced-out friend as always.
I love you to bits, truly, but if you get in my way on the board I'll run you over without an ounce of guilt.
Urban legend: once, a eurogamer took their turn in under five minutes without asking anyone to re-explain the rules.
Time is relative. A minute waiting for the bus is eternal; a minute thinking about your move is an insult to the rest of the table. Come on, already!
I'm begging you, move your piece already. My grandkids need to inherit this game night sometime this century.
I'm not zoning out, I'm calculating the next 47 variables of the game. Let me crunch in peace.
I don't have bad luck with dice, it's the dice that don't have the faintest clue what high strategy is.
Luck doesn't exist. The dice have just had it out for me since the night began.
The worst phrase in the universe: 'It's just a game', right after they beat you by a single miserable victory point.
If life gives you lemons... check whether they trade well in the commerce phase or if you can offload them on someone else.
Life is short, take the extra turn and may God help you.
I'm not addicted to board games. I just have a very intense and expensive love affair with cardboard, plastic, and that new-box smell.
Behind every great board gamer... is a mountain of discarded card sleeves and a thousand zip bags that came from who-knows-where.
On this site we don't sell games, we sell the perfect excuse to leave your phone on read for three hours and actually see each other's faces.
